_comment: Measured against LIVE PRODUCTION after the promotion on 2026-08-01, not modelled and not extrapolated. Byte counts are wire bytes: fetched twice, once with Accept-Encoding: identity and once with gzip, writing the raw stream to disk and using its length (curl's size_download reports POST-decompression bytes and would show no saving at all).

host._comment: Read off the box during deploy via os.cpus()/os.totalmem() and free -m. Nothing in the repo recorded this before; the AWS report says 'read it off the box' and nobody had. This is the binding constraint on the whole app tier.
host.colocated: storefront + admin + php-fpm + 6 systemd queue workers + nginx

compression._comment: nginx had no gzip and there was no Laravel middleware, so every JSON response went out uncompressed.

conditionalRequests._comment: cache.headers:etag on the public read routes. A repeat request with If-None-Match costs headers instead of a body.

storefrontBundle._comment: The agentation dev toolbar was imported statically, so it shipped in the eager chunk graph on every route despite a hostname gate that stops it ever rendering for a customer. Before is staging's served HTML; after is production's served HTML. Both counted the same way: parse <script> tags out of the delivered HTML, fetch each chunk, sum the bytes.

opcacheValidateTimestamps._comment: Reverted. Justified as 'saves a stat() per file per request', which is wrong: opcache re-stats a file at most once per opcache.revalidate_freq seconds, default 2, so under load it amortises to nothing. Measured with an interleaved A/B because this host produced a 6.7x swing between two runs of an identical config; arms alternate each round so drift cancels, and the reported delta is the median of per-round paired differences, not a difference of means.
opcacheValidateTimestamps.verdict: reverted — no measurable gain, and it risks serving stale bytecode if a deploy fails to cycle php-fpm

deploymentIncident._comment: Recorded because it is the most expensive thing that happened during this pass and the fixes are load-bearing.
deploymentIncident.impact: storefront and admin returned 502; the API was unaffected throughout
causes: pm2 reload cannot change a running app's exec_mode, so the fork->cluster conversion silently did nothing and the cluster assert failed the deploy with the app stopped

the ecosystem files pointed logs at /var/log/pm2, which does not exist and the deploy user cannot create; PM2 treats that as a fatal start error, and it fired after pm2 delete had already removed the app
the admin's next binary is hoisted by yarn to admin-src/node_modules, so the hardcoded rest/node_modules path could never resolve
fixes: branch on exec_mode and convert with delete + start
resolve the next binary through Node's resolver instead of hardcoding a path
drop the custom log paths and use PM2's default, which always exists
restore the previous fork-mode process if the clustered start fails, so a failed deploy cannot leave the app down
readiness loop curls the port until it answers, so 'PM2 started it' is never reported as 'it serves'

deferredItemsCompleted._comment: The five items previously listed as 'not done, deliberately'. Each was taken to a measurement rather than an opinion. Two shipped, two are null results that were NOT shipped, and one turned out to rest on a wrong premise.

opcachePreload.verdict: MEASURED GOOD LOCALLY, BUT NOT ACTIVE ON PRODUCTION — the dry run caught a segfault and disabled it
opcachePreload.productionOutcome: The deploy's pre-flight compile of preload.php SEGFAULTED on the production PHP 8.1 build: 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)'. The guard did exactly its job — the directive was never written, php-fpm restarted normally, and all three services stayed up (API 200, storefront 200, admin 307). Without that dry run, php-fpm's master would have segfaulted at startup and the box would have served nothing at all.
opcachePreload.productionStatus: preload OFF; the machinery stays in place and is self-enabling — if the underlying build issue is fixed, the next deploy's dry run passes and preload turns itself on with no code change
opcachePreload.whyItMayDiffer: The A/B ran against macOS/homebrew PHP 8.1.32; production is Ubuntu PHP 8.1 with a different extension set. opcache preload is known to be sensitive to which classes can be eagerly linked, and the local run already emitted 'Can't preload unlinked class' warnings for Lighthouse and Excel interfaces. Narrowing the include list further may make it viable, but each attempt costs a production deploy and the upside is 3.3%.
opcachePreload.method: interleaved A/B, 8 rounds x 220 requests, arms alternated per round, paired medians
opcachePreload.note: p95 improves 20%, and 7/8 one-directional is what separates this from the reverted changes (validate_timestamps won 2/8, the provider cull 4/6). Preloads 1,587 files / 1,573 classes for 19.3MB. Ships behind a dry run AND a post-restart rollback, because a fatal in a preload script stops php-fpm from starting at all — which the first version did, by referencing STDERR.

serviceProviders.claimBefore: 81 boot-time service providers were 'the most promising remaining lever on the framework floor'
serviceProviders.reality: Production installs with --no-dev, so only 3 of the discovered providers are dev-only; the real count is ~94, not 81. A lean manifest dropping 19 providers (7 unused payment gateways for markets this business does not serve, plus Lighthouse/GraphQL which nothing calls) boots fine at HTTP 200.
serviceProviders.note: Both arms are coin flips, and per-round deltas swing from -223ms to +65ms — pure host noise. With warm opcache, provider registration is cheap object construction; the expensive part (compiling files) is already cached, and Laravel defers most providers anyway. Not worth editing a vendored package's payment code for 0%.

rawImgTagsAndCls.verdict: PREMISE WAS WRONG — fixed the real cause instead
rawImgTagsAndCls.claimBefore: 48 raw tags serving unresized S3 originals cause the 0.595 search-desktop CLS
rawImgTagsAndCls.reality: Measured with PerformanceObserver on layout-shift entries: NOT ONE shifting element is an . All six are DIVs. The images already sit in containers with reserved height.
rawImgTagsAndCls.actualCause: FeaturedPlants loads Carousel and the product card via dynamic(ssr:false) with NO loading fallback, so both render null until their chunks arrive. The section is ~597px tall, sitting directly above the result count and product grid, so each null render moved the whole page.
rawImgTagsAndCls.note: Fixed by giving both dynamic imports the same skeleton row the data-loading branch already used. Still dynamic, not static — a static card import is the documented React 19 hydration-loop trap here. Residual 0.383 is above the 0.1 'good' threshold and still worth chasing; the remaining shift has the same signature, so more of the section's states differ in height. Staging cannot test this path at all: its best-selling-plants API returns 0 products, so the section returns null there.

redis.verdict: NOT ENABLED — the only measurement available says it is SLOWER
redis.why: config/database.php defaults REDIS_CLIENT to 'phpredis' (the C extension), but that extension is installed NOWHERE — not locally, not on production. The measurement therefore ran on predis, which parses the Redis protocol in userland PHP on every cache read, while the MySQL connection is already open and pooled for the request.
redis.blocked: The C client could not be measured on this machine: pecl's channel is broken (XML parse error) and the brew formula requires replacing the PHP build. Enabling Redis on production would be shipping an unmeasured change against the only evidence available.
redis.recommendation: Install php8.1-redis on the box and re-measure BEFORE switching CACHE_DRIVER. Note production cannot be load-tested by instruction, so this needs a like-for-like rig with the extension present.

loadLadderCeiling.verdict: MEASURED — the theory was right, and is now a number
loadLadderCeiling.claimBefore: 50,000 concurrent is not achievable from this machine — 16,384 ephemeral ports caps it
loadLadderCeiling.note: Within 0.3% of the theoretical 16,384, so the claim held. Also worth recording: kern.ipc.somaxconn is 128 on this box, which the reports never mentioned and which is a far tighter limit than the port range for BURST accepts — though it did not bite for held connections. Going past 16,340 needs additional source IPs (loopback aliases), which requires sudo that is not available in this session. It would also be pointless: the app saturates at ~444 RPS around 10 VUs, so 50k concurrent measures the laptop's socket handling, not the application.

latentBugFound._comment: Unrelated to this pass, found by reading the deploy log during the incident.
latentBugFound.bug: the appDir patch in both production workflows has been a silent no-op since 2026-07-14
latentBugFound.detail: required-server-files.json is pretty-printed ('"appDir": "..."' with a space) while the sed pattern had none, so it never matched; the admin's echo printed a hardcoded success message either way
latentBugFound.fix: apply the edit as JSON and assert the result
